references.text: Detailed laws about the peace offering (שְׁלָמִים), describing the various types of peace offerings and how they are to be eaten.
The requirement that the sacrificial animal must be without blemish (תָּמִים) when someone brings a peace offering to the Lord.
Parallel to the burnt offering from cattle (מִן־הַבָּקָר), which also had to be without blemish.
Continuation of the law concerning peace offerings, where small livestock (sheep or goats) may also be used as sacrifices.
The requirement for a blameless animal (תָּמִים) at the Passover celebration, showing the consistent principle of perfect sacrificial animals.
The peace offering (שְׁלָמִים) was used during the covenant-making at Sinai.
The peace offering mentioned as one of the types of offerings that the Israelites were to bring.
The peace offering as part of worship and joy in the presence of the Lord.
Christ is our peace (εἰρήνη), fulfilling the symbolism of the peace offering regarding fellowship between God and humanity.
Christ established peace through the blood of the cross, which is the fulfillment of what the peace offering pointed toward.
Lev 22:19 states the general principle of blamelessness that Lev 3:1 applies specifically to the peace offering.
Num 6:14 demonstrates the application of the requirement for a blameless animal for the peace offering in the law of the Nazirite.
